listening_script.speed_note: Read aloud at a normal, clear pace (85 wpm). Pause 2–3 seconds between sentences. Read the full text twice before students answer questions.
listening_script.text:
A FOOD CHAIN shows how energy moves from one living thing to another.
THE PARTS OF A FOOD CHAIN:
1. PRODUCER (makes food)
- Plants make food through photosynthesis
- Example: grass, trees, algae
2. PRIMARY CONSUMER (eats producers)
- Herbivores eat plants
- Example: rabbit, deer, caterpillar
3. SECONDARY CONSUMER (eats primary consumers)
- Carnivores eat other animals
- Example: snake, frog, small birds
4. TERTIARY CONSUMER (top predator)
- Eats secondary consumers
- Example: eagle, lion, shark
EXAMPLE FOOD CHAIN:
Grass → Rabbit → Snake → Eagle
Energy flows from the sun to producers to consumers.
Each step is called a TROPHIC LEVEL.
If one part of the food chain disappears, the whole chain is affected!
Science Vocabulary:
dictation: A FOOD CHAIN shows how energy moves from one living thing to another.

THE PARTS OF A FOOD CHAIN:
1.
Each step is called a TROPHIC LEVEL.
